newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Perennial seen weak in Monday debut.
newsitem.headline: HK's Perennial seen weak in Monday debut.

text.p: Shares of cable and wire manufacturer Perennial International Ltd are seen making a weak debut on Monday after a cool response to its initial public offering (IPO) of shares in Hong Kong, analysts said on Friday.
"I don't expect a strong rally in view of its cool IPO response," said a research manager at a local brokerage. "The company's fundamentals also did not sound very exciting."
Perennial offered 60 million shares, consisting of 40 million new shares and 20 million existing shares, at HK$1.07 each. The IPO was about 2.03 times subscribed.
Brokers said short-term investors were likely to take profit on the first day of trading, putting pressure on the price.

Analysts said the narrow gap between Perennial's price to earnings multiple of 5.67 times on a weighted average basis and the 9.63 times of counterpart Solartech International Holdings Ltd led to an expectation of limited room on the upside, which was seen reducing investor interest in the stock.
Perennial said proceeds of the issue would be used to boost production capacity, buy machinery, repay debt and for working capital.
